plan: 2 Samuel 6:12a; 1 Chronicles 15:1-28; 2 Samuel 6:12b-15, 16; 1 Chronicles 15:29; 2 Samuel 6:17-19a; 1 Chronicles 16:1-6, 7-36, 37-42, 43; 2 Samuel 6:19b-23

readings.title: Preparing for the Ark
readings.subtitle: The Lĕwites are Appointed
readings.text: [2 Samuel 6:12] And it was reported to Sovereign Dawiḏ, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed <dn>את</dn> the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and <dn>את</dn> all that belongs to him, because of the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [1 Chronicles 15:1] And he built houses for himself in the City of Dawiḏ. And he prepared a place for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and pitched a tent for it. [2] Then Dawiḏ said, “No one is to bear <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> but the Lĕwites, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has chosen them to bear <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> and to serve <dn>Him</dn> forever.” [3] And Dawiḏ gathered all Yisra’ĕl to Yerushalayim, to bring up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to its place, which he had prepared for it. [4] And Dawiḏ assembled <dn>את</dn> the children of Aharon and <dn>את</dn> the Lĕwites: [5] of the sons of Qehath, Uri’ĕl the chief, and one hundred and twenty of his brothers; [6] of the sons of Merari, Asayah the chief, and two hundred and twenty of his brothers; [7] of the sons of Gĕreshom, Yo’ĕl the chief, and one hundred and thirty of his brothers; [8] of the sons of Elitsaphan, Shemayah the chief, and two hundred of his brothers; [9] of the sons of Ḥeḇron, Eli’ĕl the chief, and eighty of his brothers; [10] of the sons of Uzziy’ĕl, Amminaḏaḇ the chief, and one hundred and twelve of his brothers. [11] And Dawiḏ called for Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the priests, and for the Lĕwites, for Uri’ĕl, Asayah, and Yo’ĕl, Shemayah, and Eli’ĕl, and Amminaḏaḇ, [12] and said to them, “You are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Lĕwites. Set yourselves apart, you and your brothers, and you shall bring up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl to the place I have prepared for it. [13] “Because you did not do it the first time, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> broke out against us, because we did not seek <dn>Him</dn> according to the right-ruling.” [14] So the priests and the Lĕwites set themselves apart to bring up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl. [15] And the children of the Lĕwites bore <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> on their shoulders, by its poles, as Mosheh had commanded according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [16] And Dawiḏ spoke to the leaders of the Lĕwites to appoint <dn>את</dn> their brothers, the singers, with instruments of song, harps, and lyres, and cymbals, to sound aloud, to lift up the voice with joy. [17] And the Lĕwites appointed <dn>את</dn> Hĕman son of Yo’ĕl, and of his brothers, <dn>את</dn> Asaph son of Bereḵyah. And of their brothers, the sons of Merari, <dn>את</dn> Ěythan son of Qushayah. [18] And with them their brothers of the second rank: Zeḵaryahu, Bĕn, and Ya‛azi’ĕl, and Shemiramoth, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Unni, Eli’aḇ, and Benayahu, and Ma‛asĕyahu, and Mattithyahu, and Eliphelĕhu, and Miqnĕyahu, and Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, and Ye‛i’ĕl, the gatekeepers; [19] and the singers, Hĕman, Asaph, and Ěythan, with bronze cymbals to sound aloud; [20] and Zeḵaryah, and Azi’ĕl, and Shemiramoth, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Unni, and Eli’aḇ, and Ma‛asĕyahu, and Benayahu, with lyres according to Alamoth; [21] and Mattithyahu, and Eliphelĕhu, and Miqnĕyahu, and Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, and Ye‛i’ĕl, and Azazyahu, to direct with harps on the Sheminith; [22] and Kenanyahu, leader of the Lĕwites, was instructor in song, because he was understanding; [23] and Bereḵyah and Elqanah were gatekeepers for the ark; [24] and Sheḇanyahu, and Yoshaphat, and Nethan’ĕl, and Amasay, and Zeḵaryahu, and Benayahu, and Eli‛ezer, the priests, were to blow the trumpets before the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and Yeḥiyah, gatekeepers for the ark. [25] So Dawiḏ, and the elders of Yisra’ĕl, and the commanders over thousands, went to bring up <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom with joy. [26] And it came to be, when <dn>Elohim</dn> helped the Lĕwites who bore the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that they offered seven bulls and seven rams. [27] And Dawiḏ was dressed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Lĕwites who bore the ark, and the singers, and Kenanyahu the music leader with the singers. And Dawiḏ wore a linen shoulder garment. [28] And all Yisra’ĕl brought up <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with shouting and with the sound of the horn, with trumpets and with cymbals, sounding aloud with lyres and harps.

readings.title: Bringing the Ark With Joy
readings.subtitle: Dawiḏ Dances Before YeHoVaH
readings.text: [2 Samuel 6:12] So Dawiḏ went and brought up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> from the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom to the City of Dawiḏ with gladness. [13] And it came to be, when those bearing the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had gone six steps, that he slaughtered a bull and a fatted sheep. [14] And Dawiḏ danced before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with all his might. And Dawiḏ was wearing a linen shoulder garment. [15] Thus Dawiḏ and all the house of Yisra’ĕl brought up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with shouting and with the sound of a ram’s horn. [16] And it came to be, as the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came into the City of Dawiḏ, that Miḵal, Sha’ul’s daughter, looked through a window and saw <dn>את</dn> Sovereign Dawiḏ leaping and dancing before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and she despised him in her heart. [1 Chronicles 15:29] And it came to be, as the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to the City of Dawiḏ, that Miḵal, daughter of Sha’ul, looking through a window, saw <dn>את</dn> Sovereign Dawiḏ dancing and playing. And she despised him in her heart.

readings.title: Offerings and Blessings
readings.subtitle: Ministers Appointed for the Ark
readings.text: [2 Samuel 6:17] And they brought <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and set it in its place in the midst of the tent that Dawiḏ had pitched for it. And Dawiḏ brought burnt offerings before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and peace offerings. [18] And when Dawiḏ had finished bringing burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed <dn>את</dn> the people in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [19] And he distributed to all the people, to the entire crowd of Yisra’ĕl, from man to woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, and a measure of date-wine, and a cake of raisins. [1 Chronicles 16:1] And they brought <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and set it in the midst of the tent that Dawiḏ had pitched for it. And they brought burnt offerings and peace offerings before <dn>Elohim</dn>. [2] And when Dawiḏ had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed <dn>את</dn> the people in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] And he distributed to everyone of Yisra’ĕl, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, and a measure of date-wine, and a cake of raisins. [4] And he appointed some of the Lĕwites to serve before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to bring to remembrance, and to thank, and to praise <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl: [5] Asaph the chief, and next to him Zeḵaryah, then Ye‛i’ĕl, and Shemiramoth, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Mattithyahu, and Eli’aḇ, and Benayahu, and Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, and Ye‛i’ĕl, with instruments of lyres and harps, but Asaph was sounding the cymbals; [6] and Benayahu and Yaḥazi’ĕl the priests, continually with trumpets before the ark of the covenant of <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: Dawiḏ’s Psalm of Thanksgiving
readings.subtitle: Declare His Esteem Among the Nations
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 16:7] Then on that day Dawiḏ first gave into the hand of Asaph and his brothers to give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: [8] Give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, call upon <dn>His</dn> Name, make known <dn>His</dn> deeds among the peoples! [9] Sing to <dn>Him</dn>, sing praise to <dn>Him</dn>, speak of all <dn>His</dn> wonders! [10] Boast in <dn>His</dn> set-apart Name, let the hearts of those seeking <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rejoice! [11] Seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>His</dn> strength, seek <dn>His</dn> face continually! [12] Remember <dn>His</dn> wonders which <dn>He</dn> has done, <dn>His</dn> signs and the right-rulings of <dn>His</dn> mouth, [13] O seed of Yisra’ĕl <dn>His</dn> servant, children of Ya‛aqoḇ, <dn>His</dn> chosen ones! [14] <dn>He</dn> is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>His</dn> right-rulings are in all the earth. [15] Remember <dn>His</dn> covenant forever, the word <dn>He</dn> commanded, for a thousand generations, [16] which <dn>He</dn> made with Aḇraham, and <dn>His</dn> oath to Yitsḥaq, [17] and <dn>He</dn> established it to Ya‛aqoḇ for a law, to Yisra’ĕl as an everlasting covenant, [18] saying, <dq>“To you <dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> the land of Kena‛an, the portion of your inheritance,”</dq> [19] when you were but few in number, few indeed, and sojourners in it. [20] And they went up and down, from one nation to another, and from one kingdom to another people. [21] <dn>He</dn> allowed no one to oppress them, and <dn>He</dn> reproved sovereigns for their sakes, saying, [22] <dq>“Do not touch <dn>My</dn> anointed ones, and do <dn>My</dn> prophets no evil.”</dq> [23] Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all the earth; proclaim <dn>His</dn> deliverance from day to day. [24] Declare <dn>His</dn> esteem among the nations, <dn>His</dn> wonders among all peoples. [25] For great is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and greatly to be praised. And <dn>He</dn> is to be feared above all mighty ones. [26] For all the mighty ones of the peoples are matters of naught, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made the heavens. [27] Excellency and splendour are before <dn>Him</dn>, strength and gladness are in <dn>His</dn> place. [28] Ascribe to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O clans of the peoples, ascribe to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> esteem and strength. [29] Ascribe to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the esteem of <dn>His</dn> Name; bring an offering, and come before <dn>Him</dn>; bow yourself to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the splendour of set-apartness! [30] Tremble before <dn>Him</dn>, all the earth. The world also is firmly established, immovable. [31] Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad; and let them say among the nations, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall reign.” [32] Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; let the field rejoice, and all that is in it. [33] Let the trees of the forest then sing before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> shall come to judge the earth. [34] Give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is good, for <dn>His</dn> kindness is everlasting! [35] And say, “Save us, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of our deliverance; and gather us together, and deliver us from the nations, to give thanks to <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Name, and to boast in <dn>Your</dn> praise.” [36] Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl from everlasting to everlasting! And all the people said, “Amĕn!” and praised <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Miḵal’s Contempt
readings.subtitle: Dawiḏ Defends His Rejoicing
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 16:37] So he left <dn>את</dn> Asaph and <dn>את</dn> his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to serve before the ark continually, as every day’s work required; [38] and <dn>את</dn> Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom with his sixty-eight brothers, including Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom son of Yeḏuthun, and Ḥosah, to be gatekeepers; [39] and <dn>את</dn> Tsaḏoq the priest and his brothers the priests, before the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at the high place that was at Giḇ‛on, [40] to offer burnt offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the slaughter-place of burnt offering continually, morning and evening, and to do according to all that is written in the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> commanded Yisra’ĕl; [41] and with them Hĕman and Yeḏuthun and the rest who were chosen, who were designated by name, to give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because <dn>His</dn> kindness is everlasting; [42] and with them Hĕman and Yeḏuthun, to sound aloud with trumpets and cymbals and instruments for the songs of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the sons of Yeḏuthun for the gate. [43] And all the people went, each one to his house, and Dawiḏ returned to bless <dn>את</dn> his house. [2 Samuel 6:19] Then all the people left, each one to his house. [20] And Dawiḏ returned to bless <dn>את</dn> his household. And Miḵal the daughter of Sha’ul came out to meet Dawiḏ, and said, “How esteemed was the sovereign of Yisra’ĕl today, uncovering himself today in the eyes of the female servants of his servants, as one of the foolish ones shamelessly uncovers himself!” [21] And Dawiḏ said to Miḵal, “Before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who chose me instead of your father and all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, over Yisra’ĕl – so I danced before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [22] “And I shall be even more lightly esteemed than this, and shall be humble in my own eyes. But as for the female servants of whom you have spoken, by them I shall be esteemed.” [23] And Miḵal the daughter of Sha’ul had no children to the day of her death.
